blocks.content: With the slow region isolated, open a healthy region's flame graph first, then the expensive one, so the difference is easier to see. A flame graph is a hierarchical view of call stacks. Horizontally, wider nodes cost more. Vertically, each level is a caller–callee relationship: the root sits at the top, and callees stack beneath their callers. **Self** time is spent in the function itself; **total** time is the function plus its callees. For more, see Flame graphs and self vs. total metrics. To explore flame graphs, complete the following steps:

blocks.reftarget: section[data-testid='data-testid Panel header ap-south-1'] button[aria-label='Flame graph']
blocks.content: Select **Flame graph** for `ap-south-1`, a healthier region.
Take a look at how CPU time is distributed across the call stack. Keep this picture in mind as a baseline.
In the **Filters** bar, change the `region` filter from `ap-south-1` to `eu-west-1`.
Compared with `ap-south-1`, a lot more time is spent in functions related to regex.
Eye-balling two flame graphs works, but there's an easier way. Return to the grouped **region** view to set up a Diff.
Next, use a Diff flame graph to compare the regions together.
